diagnostic_evidence.quote: (h_z)_* \pi = \frac{1}{z} \pi \quad \text{for all } z \in \mathbb{R}^\times.
\Pi(x, t) = \frac{1}{t} \Lambda(x) + \frac{\partial}{\partial t} \wedge E(x),
(h_z)_*X = z^kX.

issues.failure_explanation: With h_z(x,t)=(x,zt), the pushforward is (h_z)_*\Pi(x,s)=Th_z(\Pi(x,s/z)) = (z/s)\Lambda + z\,\partial_t\wedge E = z\,\Pi(x,s). So the asserted 'direct computation' is false: the Poissonization satisfies (h_z)_*\Pi = z\Pi, i.e. it is 1-homogeneous in the sense of (vf k-homoge), not -1-homogeneous as the Definition of homogeneous Poisson manifold requires. The same sign mismatch appears with the symplectic convention: h_z^*\omega=z\omega implies (h_z)_*\omega^{-1}=z\,\omega^{-1} (e.g. T^*P with the lift (eq: cotangent lift)), so a homogeneous symplectic manifold would not be a homogeneous Poisson manifold under the stated definition, and Hamiltonian vector fields of 1-homogeneous functions would be (-2)-homogeneous rather than 0-homogeneous as used throughout.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the defining condition by (h_z)_*\pi = z\pi (1-homogeneous bivector in the paper's convention, corresponding to the bracket having weight -1) and correct the computation in the proof of prop:added-1 accordingly; all later uses assume this corrected convention.
issues.overall_effect: As literally stated, the Poissonization and symplectizations are not 'homogeneous Poisson manifolds', so the definitional bridge between Jacobi manifolds and homogeneous Poisson manifolds (and the objects to which Sections 4-6 apply) is inconsistent.
issues.title: Poissonization is 1-homogeneous, not (-1)-homogeneous, under the paper's own pushforward convention
issues.why_classification: A single sign/convention correction restores consistency; no result or construction changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for which $(\omega_0)_{|N} =(\omega_1)_{|N} $
So, it follows that $\beta_{|X}=0$ and $\beta$ is $1$-homogeneous.
the symplectic form $\Omega = \int_0^1(\phi^s_X)^*\omega_{can} ds$ is also $1$-homogeneous

issues.failure_explanation: The Darboux–Weinstein theorem (as proved in Appendix A, where \beta|_N=0 is deduced from \sigma=\omega_0-\omega_1 vanishing on T_NM) requires the two forms to coincide on all tangent vectors at points of N. Along the zero section, d\phi^s_X(\partial_{\xi_j}) = \partial_{\xi_j} + s\Pi^{ij}\partial_{y_i}, so (\phi^s_X)^*\omega_{can}(\partial_{\xi_j},\partial_{\xi_k}) = -2s\Pi^{jk} and \Omega(\partial_{\xi_j},\partial_{\xi_k}) = -\Pi^{jk} \neq 0 = \omega_{can}(\partial_{\xi_j},\partial_{\xi_k}) whenever \Pi\neq 0. Hence the hypothesis of thm: Darboux-Weinstein is violated and the existence of the homogeneous \Psi (the Karasev realization used to define \alpha,\beta in thm: bi-realization) is not established by the cited theorem.

failure_location.quote: By the homogeneous Darboux-Weinstein Theorem (\ref{thm: Darboux-Weinstein}), there exists $\Psi:T^*P\rightarrow T^*P$ such that $\omega_{can} = \Psi^*\Omega$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Invoke instead the homogeneous Weinstein Lagrangian neighborhood theorem (thm: Weinstein lagrangian), noting that the zero section is Lagrangian for both \omega_{can} and \Omega (since \phi^s_X fixes it pointwise) and is homogeneous; this yields a homogeneous \Psi fixing the zero section with \Psi^*\Omega=\omega_{can}.
issues.overall_effect: The passage from the Weinstein realization to the canonical-form (Karasev) homogeneous bi-realization, on which the construction of Sections 4.3-6 relies, is not justified as written.
issues.title: Darboux–Weinstein theorem invoked although \Omega and \omega_{can} do not agree along the zero section
issues.why_classification: The correct tool is already proved in the paper and applies directly; only the citation and a one-line verification change.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \alpha^i(y,\xi) = y^i + \frac{1}{2}\pi^{vi}\xi_v

X = \frac{1}{t}\left(\xi_{q^i} + p_i\xi_z\right)\frac{\partial}{\partial p_i} - \frac{1}{t}\xi_{p_i}\frac{\partial}{\partial q^i} + \left(\xi_t-\frac{p_i}{t}\xi_{p_i} \right)\frac{\partial}{\partial z} - \xi_z\frac{\partial}{\partial t}.

issues.failure_explanation: The truncation (eq: approximation alpha) gives \alpha = y + \tfrac12\Pi^\sharp(\xi), where \Pi^\sharp(\xi) is the base part of the spray displayed just before: (\dot q,\dot p,\dot z,\dot t) = (-\xi_p/t, (\xi_q+p\xi_z)/t, \xi_t - p\xi_p/t, -\xi_z). The displayed \alpha has q-, p- and z-components equal to y - \tfrac12\Pi^\sharp(\xi) but t-component t - \tfrac12\xi_z = y + \tfrac12\Pi^\sharp(\xi). With either overall sign convention one component has the wrong sign, so the displayed maps are not first-order truncations of a realization: neither \alpha nor \beta is Poisson/anti-Poisson to the claimed order (the mixed {z,t}-type brackets come out with the wrong sign).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the sign of the \xi_z term in the t-component (or of the other three components) in both displayed maps, consistently with \alpha = y + \tfrac12\Pi^\sharp(\xi).
issues.overall_effect: The only explicit bi-realization computed in the paper (and the formulas one would use in a concrete JHI) is incorrect as written; the same defect propagates to eq: bi-realization example2.
issues.title: Explicit second-order realization maps have inconsistent signs between the t-component and the other components
issues.why_classification: A local sign correction in an example; no general result depends on the explicit formula.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we call variation functions to any time-dependent functions $(f_s)_{s\in I}$ such that $df_s = \xi_s$

issues.failure_explanation: Variation functions are only determined up to additive constants (on each component). If \xi_s = 0 and f_s = 1, then \xi_s is 1-homogeneous but h_z^*f_s = 1 \neq z f_s, so the 'only if' direction is false for arbitrary variation functions; the corollary is stated without proof.

failure_location.quote: Then $\xi_s$ are $1$-homogeneous if and only if $f_s$ are $1$-homogeneous.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate as: \xi_s is 1-homogeneous iff there exists a 1-homogeneous choice of variation function f_s (on connected components, h_z^*f_s - z f_s = k(z-1) for a constant k, so f_s + k works).
issues.overall_effect: As stated the corollary is false; what is true (and needed) is that 1-homogeneous exact \xi_s admit a 1-homogeneous primitive.
issues.title: Corollary: homogeneity of variation forms does not force homogeneity of given variation functions
issues.why_classification: Only a quantifier ('there exist') needs correction with a two-line argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Moreover, given a bisection $L$, the inverse restricted to $L$, $\alpha^{-1}_{|L}$ is also homogeneous: $\alpha^{-1}_{|L}\circ h_z = T^*h_z\circ \alpha^{-1}_{|L}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition assumes only that L is a Lagrangian bisection, yet concludes \phi_L is homogeneous. The preceding remark's derivation of homogeneity of \alpha^{-1}|_L uses (implicitly) that L is T^*h_z-invariant. For a non-invariant Lagrangian bisection, e.g. L_s = \phi^s_{\alpha^*F}(\sigma(P)) for a non-homogeneous F, \phi_L is the (non-homogeneous) flow of F, so (1) fails.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that L is a homogeneous (T^*h_z-invariant) Lagrangian bisection, both in the remark and in prop:added-4.
issues.overall_effect: Statement (1) is false without the homogeneity hypothesis on L; the intended use (homogeneous Lagrangian bisections) is unaffected once the hypothesis is added.
issues.title: Homogeneity of the induced Poisson diffeomorphism requires the bisection to be homogeneous
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard hypothesis that all subsequent uses already satisfy restores the result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the induced map $\varphi_L = \beta\circ \alpha^{-1}_{|L}$ defines a Poisson diffeomorphism

\item $\alpha$ is a Poisson map,
    \item $\beta$ is an anti-Poisson map,
    \item the fibers of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are symplectic orthogonal to each other.

issues.failure_explanation: Since \alpha is Poisson, \alpha\circ\phi^s_{\alpha^*H} = \phi^s_H\circ\alpha (which gives item 2). Since X_{\alpha^*H} is \omega-orthogonal to \ker d\alpha, it lies in \ker d\beta, so \beta\circ\phi^s_{\alpha^*H}=\beta. For x\in P the unique point of L_s over x under \alpha is \phi^s_{\alpha^*H}(\sigma(\phi^{-s}_H x)), whose \beta-image is \phi^{-s}_H(x). Hence \varphi_{L_s} = \beta\circ\alpha^{-1}|_{L_s} = \phi^{-s}_H, contradicting item 3 as stated with the paper's conventions for \alpha,\beta and \varphi_L.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either define \varphi_L = \alpha\circ\beta^{-1}|_L (or take \beta Poisson and \alpha anti-Poisson), or state item 3 as \varphi_{L_s} = \phi^{-s}_H, and adjust the integrator remark accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The map produced from the bisection L_s is the time-reversed flow; the integrator defined by x\mapsto\beta\circ(\alpha|_{L_{\Delta t}})^{-1}(x) approximates the flow of -H^P rather than H^P unless conventions are aligned.
issues.title: Item 3 of the cited flow theorem yields \phi_H^{-s}, not \phi_H^s, with the paper's conventions
issues.why_classification: A convention/sign alignment fixes the statement with no loss of content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This grants the existence of JHI's, constructed as explained above.
provides a constructive and geometrically natural method to produce structure-preserving numerical integrators for Jacobi Hamiltonian systems
Future work may focus on the development of explicit low-order JHI schemes and their analysis on concrete examples.
\item[(4)] Approximate the flow by approximating the family of homogeneous Lagrangian bisections.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims a constructive method producing JHI of order k. What is established are: homogeneity of the bi-realization, homogeneity of variation forms, and the (cited) fact that the exact family L_s = \phi^s_{\alpha^*H}(\sigma(P)) reproduces the exact flow. The key step 4 of the outlined procedure - producing a computable, homogeneous, exact family of Lagrangian bisections whose variation functions agree with H^P to order k, and proving that \varphi_{L_s} is then the time-s flow of a homogeneous \mathcal{H}_s with \mathcal{H}_s = H^P + o(s^{k-1}) - is neither carried out nor supported by a stated result (the required relation between variation functions and the modified Hamiltonian is not proved or precisely cited in the homogeneous setting; the sentence does not even assume homogeneity of the family). The only 'existence' obtained is the trivial one (the exact flow itself satisfies the definition of a hPHI), so the prose claims of a constructive method and of a new class of numerical schemes exceed the formal content.

failure_location.quote: Given an exact smooth family of Lagrangian bisections such that $L_0$ is the zero section, constructing a suitable approximation of the variation functions $(\mathcal{H}_s)_s$ that coincides with $ H^P$ of order $k$, the induced family of diffeomorphisms $(\varphi_{L_s})_{s\in I}$ is a homogeneous Hamiltonian Poisson integrator of order $k$ for $H^P$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either add a result (e.g. a homogeneous version of the PHI construction via truncated solutions of (eq: H-J), verifying homogeneity, Lagrangian-bisection property, exactness and the order-k relation between variation functions and \mathcal{H}_s), or weaken the claims to an outline/framework whose realization as a numerical scheme is left open.
issues.overall_effect: The central advertised deliverable (a method producing order-k Jacobi Hamiltonian integrators) rests on an unproved step; no non-trivial JHI is exhibited or shown to exist.
issues.title: Existence and construction of order-k homogeneous Poisson/Jacobi Hamiltonian integrators is asserted, not established
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial argument (adapting the PHI approximation theorem with homogeneity checks) is needed; otherwise the main constructive claim must be downgraded, though the structural results survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: X_H = \Lambda(\cdot,dH) - HE(\cdot)
\item $\mathcal{H}_s = H^J + o(s^{k-1})$,

issues.failure_explanation: For a Jacobi Hamiltonian, X_H(H) = \Lambda(dH,dH) - H E(H) = -H E(H), which is nonzero in general (e.g. contact dynamics are dissipative), so the exact flow does not preserve H and no consistent integrator can. The paper's own definition of a JHI only asks that the modified Hamiltonian agree with H^J to order k, not that H be preserved.

failure_location.quote: This approach preserves not only the Jacobi structure and the Hamiltonian, but also the induced foliation and Casimir functions

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove 'and the Hamiltonian' or replace it by a statement that the integrator is the flow of a modified Hamiltonian agreeing with H to the given order.
issues.overall_effect: The stated guarantee 'preserves the Hamiltonian' is false/unsupported for Jacobi systems with E(H)\neq 0; only structure (bracket), foliation and Casimir preservation are supported by the construction.
issues.title: Conclusion claims preservation of the Hamiltonian, which fails even for exact Jacobi dynamics
issues.why_classification: A wording correction with no effect on any formal result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consider also the Poincar\'{e}-Cartan 1-form $\eta_{PC}= p_idq^i - Hdt$.
p_idq^i + Hdt -(P_idQ^i + Kdt) = dF_1,

issues.failure_explanation: The derivation requires the transformation to preserve d\eta_{PC} with \eta_{PC} = p\,dq - H\,dt, i.e. p\,dq - H\,dt - (P\,dQ - K\,dt) = dF_1, which gives K = H + \partial_t F_1 and, for K=0, the Hamilton–Jacobi equation H(q,\partial_q S,t) + \partial_t S = 0. The paper instead writes +H\,dt and -K\,dt, obtaining K = H - \partial_t F_1 and (eq: H-J) with the opposite sign. Solutions of (eq: H-J) generate the flow of -H (time-reversed dynamics), so the Lagrangian bisections \Psi^{-1}(\underline{d\mathbf{S}_t}) used in Section 5 do not correspond to the flow of H as claimed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the sign in the generating-function identity and state (eq: H-J) as H(q,\partial_q\mathbf{S}_t,t) + \partial_t\mathbf{S}_t = 0 (or consistently redefine \eta_{PC}).
issues.overall_effect: The families of Lagrangian submanifolds built from solutions of (eq: H-J) correspond to the flow of -H; all statements relating them to \phi^t_H carry an unaccounted sign.
issues.title: Sign error in the derivation of the homogeneous Hamilton–Jacobi equation
issues.why_classification: A local sign correction; the homogeneity analysis and all constructions survive unchanged.
